scope: Read the six complete routed source diffs, preparation anchors, actual-module Node checks, recorder entry/exit/metadata wrappers and prepared mounted-browser equivalence test.
Independent focused execution covers actual analysis modules, actual Sparkline module with fake uPlot, actual native delegation helper and actual subscriber wrapper.
This review checks admitted production objects and call paths. It does not assert observational equivalence for arbitrary accessor/proxy substitutions or eliminate instrumentation timing effects.

findings.subject: J-before-E acquisition and reduction
findings.detail: The original J getter is followed by its availability check and full reduction before the original E getter. Both ordinary demands remain, including missing/pending J; a throwing J getter still prevents E. New scalar descriptor reads make no bridge/native request and retain no field payload. The 48-case full-module comparison includes N=33/97, RF/light/sound/unrelated, signed/zero/empty/missing J/missing E and E-call invalidation of J arrays.

findings.subject: Scientific values and cache domain
findings.detail: No channel selection, sample validation, finite arithmetic, quadrature/Fourier reduction, preparation, cache key, output object or clock fallback changed in the source diff. Exact output comparisons passed. The additional basis-hit observation reads the existing cache key; it does not alter cache lifetime.

findings.subject: Return, throw, receiver and order
findings.detail: Added acquisition, retained DOM, audio and chart closures call the original operation and return its result; original thrown objects are rethrown through finally. Native delegation keeps fallback identity, native arguments and fn invocation. Sparkline invokes the existing uPlot receiver. Instrumentation faults are contained by recorder safe wrappers. DOM assignment and setData argument temporaries change evaluation ordering only relative to instrumentation/property lookup; accepted production refs/uPlot are ordinary owned properties, not adversarial accessors.

findings.subject: History, charts, controls and lifecycle
findings.detail: The diff preserves history tick gating, finite-zero directional values, buffer push formulas, chart window/copy loops, five-chart call order, control key/reseed handlers and unmount logic. Source changes wrap existing operations; registration adds only WeakMap attribution. Actual Sparkline baseline/routed arrays, receiver, window update, resize and disposal behavior match in the focused test. Full mounted WaveInfo/DOM/uPlot parity is delegated to the held-browser check and is not claimed here.

findings.subject: Original scheduled timing endpoints
findings.detail: The subscriber wrapper retains the original start performance.now call and uses its original end position for the inclusive elapsed subtraction. The root receives those exact endpoint values and the same callback sample index. Instrumentation adds elapsed work inside the interval; it does not replace the scheduled callback or infer callback time by independent-quantile subtraction. Focused actual-wrapper return/throw/sample association test passed.

findings.subject: Stage attribution interpretation
findings.detail: J/E acquisition includes new scalar metadata descriptor work; NATIVE_BOUND includes guards and JavaScript/embind return work, not isolated C++ CPU time. Worker getters time synchronous cache/demand work, not asynchronous worker computation. FOURIER extends through output assembly. The Sound controls innerHTML += operation remains inside CONTROLS inclusive time without its own DOM_SET child. RF-only attribution must not be described as exhaustive per-setter Sound attribution.

findings.subject: Observation provenance and labels
findings.detail: Owner-read tick remains separate from independently cached J/E sample times; missing payload sample metadata remains unknown. No common publication clock is invented. Existing directional-versus-magnitude/probe axis labels and direct missing-native-versus-completed-empty ambiguity are not repaired or certified by instrumentation.
